'''Mikael Kubista''' (born 13 August 1961) is a [[Czechs|Czech]]-born<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: CV |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Kubista_Mikael/CV |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref> Swedish [[chemist]] and entrepreneur who works in the field of [[molecular diagnostics]].

== Education ==
He completed his undergraduate studies at [[University of Gothenburg]], earning a B.Sc. degree in [[chemistry]] in 1984.<ref name="labgenexp9">{{cite web |title=GOTEBORGS UNIVERSITET |url=https://www.labgenexp.eu/file.php?nid=17117&oid=10850079 |website=labgenexp9 |access-date=8 March 2024}}</ref> He then pursued a Licentiate in Physical Chemistry at the Institute of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, [[Chalmers University of Technology]] in Göteborg, which he completed in 1986. Kubista obtained his Ph.D. in chemistry from Chalmers University of Technology.<ref name="labgenexp12">{{cite web |title=CHALMERS TEKNISKA HOGSCOLA |url=https://www.labgenexp.eu/file.php?nid=17117&oid=10850083 |website=labgenexp |access-date=8 March 2024}}</ref> Following his doctoral studies, he conducted postdoctoral research at [[La Trobe University]] in [[Melbourne, Australia]], and [[Yale University]] in [[New Haven, USA|New Haven, US]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=ORCID|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2940-352X|website=orcid.org|access-date=2025-12-01}}</ref> Additionally, he has held visiting professor positions at various universities, including the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland in College Park]], US, in June 2000, and the [[University of A Coruña]] in Spain, during September–November 2003 and July 2006 to June 2007.<ref name=":2" />

== Career ==

===Academic career===
Kubista began his academic career in 1991 as an assistant professor in the Department of Physical Chemistry at [[Chalmers University of Technology]].<ref name=":2" /> From 1993 to 1997, he was an associate professor in the Department of [[Biochemistry]] at the same institution. Following this, he held the position of professor in the Department of Biochemistry at Chalmers University of Technology from 1997 to 2006.<ref name=":2" />  He has served as head for a laboratory at the Biotechnology Institute, [[Czech Academy of Sciences]] since 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Laboratory of Gene Expression homepage |url=https://www.ibt.cas.cz/en/research-laboratories/laboratory-of-gene-expression/ |access-date=2025-11-06 |publisher=Institute of Biotechnology of the Czech Academy of Sciences |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2"/>

=== LightUp Technologies AB ===
In 1998 Kubista founded LightUp Technologies AB after his research finding of LightUp probes,<ref name="gene-quantification">{{cite web |title=Biomolecular Detection and Quantification |url=https://www.gene-quantification.de/qpcr-dpcr-ngs-a-journey-bdq-editorial-2015.pdf |access-date=2 January 2024 |website=gene-quantification}}</ref> a company that develops real-time PCR tests for human [[Infection|infectious diseases]].<ref name="asiraandkutir">{{Cite web |title=Mikael Kubista |url=https://www.biotechpharmasummit.com/index.php/liquid-biopsy-2020-speakers/mikael-kubista/ |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=BioTech Pharma Summit}}</ref>

=== TATAA Biocenter ===
In 2001, Kubista cofounded TATAA Biocenter, and Care Equity invested in [[TATAA Biocenter]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Madsen |first=Christian |date=2021-09-24 |title=One of the world’s best equipped laboratories for molecular analyses is expanding {{!}} Affärstidningen Näringsliv |url=https://naringsliv.se/2021-3/one-of-the-worlds-best-equipped-laboratories-for-molecular-analyses-is-expanding/ |access-date=2025-10-17 |language=sv-SE}}</ref><ref name="sositkutir">{{cite web |title=TATAA Biocenter to offer GLP services to developers of cell and gene therapies across the world |url=https://naringsliv.se/2022-4/tataa-biocenter-to-offer-glp-services-to-developers-of-cell-and-gene-therapies-across-the-world/ |access-date=28 December 2023 |website=naringsliv}}</ref> To facilitate the investment, a new holding company, Bioholdings LP, was established to acquire TATAA. During restructuring connected to TATAA’s [[COVID-19 testing]] business, Kubista and his co-founders, advised by a law firm, carried out an upstream merger between two holding entities. This violated a clause in the agreement that prohibited share transfers without written consent. In June 2023, Kubista was dismissed as CEO and forfeited the founders' shares without compensation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Göransson |first=Av Anders |date=2024-01-31 |title=Failed to read the fine print – lost his life’s work |url=https://www.lifesciencesweden.se/article/view/1078692/failed_to_read_the_fine_print_lost_his_lifes_work |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=Life Science Sweden}}</ref> Care Equity sued Kubista.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johansson |first=Joakim K. E. |date=2025-02-19 |title=Riskkapitalisten tog hans företag: "Isolerad, hotad och stämd" |url=https://www.realtid.se/juridik/riskkapitalisten-tog-hans-foretag-isolerad-hotad-och-stamd/ |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=Realtid |language=sv-SE}}</ref> As of October 2025, legal proceedings related to the merger dispute remain ongoing in the Swedish courts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mikael Kubista - the pioneering entrepreneur who lost ownership of the company he built |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/mikael-kubista-the-pioneering-entrepreneur-who-lost/id1719967972?i=1000643181930 |access-date=2025-08-20 |website=Apple Podcasts |language=en-US}}</ref> Kubista also sued the law firm for negligent advice and damages.<ref name="u838">{{cite web |last=Göransson|first=Anders|title=Partial court victory for entrepreneur who lost his company|website=Life Science Sweden|date=2024-12-19|url=https://www.lifesciencesweden.se/article/view/1137004/partial_court_victory_for_entrepreneur_who_lost_his_company|access-date=2025-11-27}}</ref>

=== Precision BioAnalytics ===
In 2025 Kubista together with Jens Björkman, Robert Sjöback and Fredrik Adlercreutz founded Precision BioAnalytics,<ref>{{Cite web |title=CCRM Nordic invests in Precision BioAnalytics |url=https://atmpsweden.se/news/ccrm-nordic-precision-bioanalytics/ |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=ATMP Sweden}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lagercrantz |first=Av Samuel |date=2025-04-28 |title=Mikael Kubista back with new venture after turbulent exit |url=https://www.lifesciencesweden.se/article/view/1160483/mikael_kubista_back_with_new_venture_after_turbulent_exit?token=5rjg0z2oj2rd4l30qsbx74rvs018pbho |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=Life Science Sweden}}</ref> around a new preanalytical procedure that increases sensitivity and improves precision of the preanalytical process in molecular analysis.<ref>{{Cite web |last=viktorwallen |date=2025-06-11 |title=Innovativ metod som förändrar den molekylära analysen |url=https://framtidensforskning.se/2025/06/11/innovativ-metod-som-forandrar-den-molekylara-analysen/ |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=Framtidens forskning |language=sv-SE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Swedish Company Boosts Molecular Diagnostics for ATMP |url=https://atmpsweden.se/news/molecular-diagnostics-atmp/ |access-date=2025-12-25 |website=ATMP Sweden}}</ref>

===Selected findings and publications===
Kubista has close to 300 publications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.webofscience.com/wos/author/record/A-5689-2008|title=Web Of Science}}</ref> 
* Studied and identified [[chromophore]]s and a variety of dyes commonly used as biomolecule labels like: tryptophan, [[DAPI]], [[fluorescein]],<ref name="sciencedirect4">{{cite journal |title=Absorption and fluorescence properties of fluorescein |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/058485399501421P |journal=Spectrochimica Acta Part A: Molecular and Biomolecular Spectroscopy |date=1995 |doi=10.1016/0584-8539(95)01421-P |access-date=2 January 2024 |last1=Sjöback |first1=Robert |last2=Nygren |first2=Jan |last3=Kubista |first3=Mikael |volume=51 |issue=6 |pages=L7–L21 |bibcode=1995AcSpA..51L...7S |url-access=subscription }}</ref> thiazole orange, and BEBO.<ref name="gene-quantification"/>
* Designed a probe that exhibit [[luminescence]] upon binding to specific nucleic acids.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1006/abio.2000.4534 | title=Light-Up Probes: Thiazole Orange-Conjugated Peptide Nucleic Acid for Detection of Target Nucleic Acid in Homogeneous Solution | date=2000 | last1=Svanvik | first1=Nicke | last2=Westman | first2=Gunnar | last3=Wang | first3=Dongyuan | last4=Kubista | first4=Mikael | journal=Analytical Biochemistry | volume=281 | issue=1 | pages=26–35 | pmid=10847607 }}</ref>
* Techniques for gene expression at the level of individual cells and subcellular compartments.<ref name="genome">{{cite journal |title=Gene expression profiling in single cells from the pancreatic islets of Langerhans reveals lognormal distribution of mRNA levels |url=https://genome.cshlp.org/content/15/10/1388.short |journal=Genome Research |date=2005 |pmid=16204192 |access-date=2 January 2024 |last1=Bengtsson |first1=M. |last2=Ståhlberg |first2=A. |last3=Rorsman |first3=P. |last4=Kubista |first4=M. |volume=15 |issue=10 |pages=1388–1392 |doi=10.1101/gr.3820805 |pmc=1240081 }}</ref>
* Discovered the Regeneration Initiating Cells (RICs) <ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sindelka |first1=Radek |last2=Naraine |first2=Ravindra |last3=Abaffy |first3=Pavel |last4=Zucha |first4=Daniel |last5=Kraus |first5=Daniel |last6=Netusil |first6=Jiri |last7=Smetana |first7=Karel |last8=Lacina |first8=Lukas |last9=Endaya |first9=Berwini Beduya |last10=Neuzil |first10=Jiri |last11=Psenicka |first11=Martin |last12=Kubista |first12=Mikael |date=2024-10-01 |title=Characterization of regeneration initiating cells during Xenopus laevis tail regeneration |journal=Genome Biology |language=en |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=251 |doi=10.1186/s13059-024-03396-3 |doi-access=free |issn=1474-760X |pmc=11443866 |pmid=39350302}}</ref>
